messages:
sophie: quick RFC — propose we normalize ingest.metadata (the freeform JSON blob) into a small set of typed columns + a lightweight metric_dimensions table. goal: cut cardinality in console dashboards and make per-route filtering fast without huge jsonb indexes.

sophie: current problem: dashboards do lots of WHERE metadata->>'region' = 'eu' or metadata->>'env' = 'prod' and we keep adding fields. queries get full jsonb scans or huge GIN indexes. costs + p95s keep creeping.

sophie: proposal: extract the 6 most-used keys (env, region, route_type, plan, sdk, tenant_tag) into columns on metrics_ingest, and move the rest into metric_dimensions (route_id, key, value) sharded by day. keep jsonb_raw untouched for fallback.

sophie: sample backfill SQL (sketch):
```sql
alter table metrics_ingest add column env text, add column region text, add column route_type text;
update metrics_ingest set env = (jsonb_raw->>'env')::text, region = (jsonb_raw->>'region')::text, route_type = (jsonb_raw->>'route_type')::text where env is null;
create index on metrics_ingest(env, region);
```

sophie: dual-write on ingest path for 30d, plus a read view that falls back to jsonb_raw for keys not present in columns.

diego: +1 for shape, big thumbs on reducing GIN usage. question: how do you plan to keep dashboards working during backfill? views? migration flags?

sophie: yeah view-based compatibility:
```sql
create view console_metrics as
select id, coalesce(env, jsonb_raw->>'env') as env, coalesce(region, jsonb_raw->>'region') as region, jsonb_raw as raw from metrics_ingest;
```
that way old queries can switch to console_metrics and be stable.

diego: perf note — creating indexes on the view won't help, so we need the actual columns populated BEFORE we switch dashboards. otherwise the view will still hit jsonb.

maya: UX side — we need a console migration status UI. customers will see sudden changes in filter cardinality. propose a small banner in dashboards that shows migration_state (notstarted / dualwrite / backfilling / complete) and an opt-in toggle for preview mode.

kevin: backfill risk: full table backfill will thrash DB during peak ingest. suggest incremental backfill by time windows with a write-lock-free approach. e.g. carve by created_at range and use parallel workers that mark progress in a control table. avoid VACUUM storms.

kevin: sample backfill controller pseudocode:
```py
while range = next_range():
  rows = select id, jsonb_raw from metrics_ingest where created_at between range.start and range.end;
  for r in rows:
    update metrics_ingest set env = r.jsonb_raw->>'env' where id = r.id and env is null;
  mark_done(range)
```

elin: for safety we should dual-write at the ingestion API layer using a feature-flag keyed by deployment. i can add a flag in the ingest-config to flip per-cluster. also add sampling for 1% to validate new columns.

elin: suggest feature-flag rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring that checks event counts per-tenant and alerts on drop > 0.5%

infra-bot: CI pipeline for migration scripts: migration SQL must pass on lint + dry-run check. recorded runtime estimate must be added to PR.

deploy-bot: canary plan: run dual-write on staging -> canary cluster (10%) -> prod alpha (50 tenants) -> prod wide. schedule off-peak initial backfills.

diego: question re: metric_dimensions table cardinality — if we materialize k/v for many keys we still get explosion. whats our cardinality cap? maybe TTL older than 90d and aggregate to label hashes?

sophie: agree. plan is to only persist non-indexed keys in metric_dimensions and add a daily compaction job that collapses low-cardinality high-cardinality combos into hashed bins and stores a mapping for debug. retention: 90d by default.

kevin: action items: 1) Sophie to open RFC PR with exact column list + sample queries (due Thu), 2) Elin to add dual-write flag and sampling in ingest service (due Mon), 3) Diego to prototype backfill controller and run on staging (due next Wed), 4) Maya to draft console migration UI mockups and banner language (due next Tue).

sophie: thanks — I'll add the migration_state field to console api and push the RFC tonight. tagging @eng-sre for review when we have backfill runbook. :thumbsup:
